explanation: The image in a plane mirror is virtual, erect same size and laterally inverted. For a plane mirror, the size of the image is equal to the size of the object.
subject: Physics

question_text: Which one of the following colours may be obtained by combining green and red colours?
explanation: Yellow colour is obtained by combining green and red colours. It is a secondary colour.
subject: Physics

question_text: Which of the following are the primary colours of light?
explanation: Primary colours of light are blue, red and green. This is the essential method used to create the precepting of a board range of colours.
subject: Physics

question_text: According to the new cartesian sign convention, which one of the following is correct in respect of the formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, where symbols have their usual meanings?
options: It applies only to spherical mirrors.
It applies only to spherical lenses.
It applies to spherical mirrors as well as spherical lenses.
correct_answer: It applies to spherical mirrors as well as spherical lenses.
explanation: For a spherical mirror, the formula showing the relationship between the distance of the object(u), the distance of the mirror (v) and the distance of the focus (f) is called the mirror formula, which is as follows: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u
subject: Physics

question_text: Movement of materials to different parts of cytoplasm and nucleus is generally carried out by
explanation: The movement of materials to different parts of the cytoplasm and nucleus is generally carried out Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER). although Golgi bodies have main role in the function of intracellular transportation. ER is the largest membrane-bound organelle in eukaryotic cells and performs a variety of essential cellular functions, including protein and lipid synthesis and biosynthesis of cell and nuclear membrane.
subject: Biology

question_text: In mitochondria, ATP synthesising chemical reactions take place in the
explanation: In eukaryotes, Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP) synthesis reaction occurs on the inner membrane of mitochondria which sides toward matrix compartment. It contains the ATP synthesis complex or oxisome or F1-particles which are the site of Electron Transportation System (ETS) of aerobic cellular espiration.
subject: Biology

question_text: Squamous epithelial cells are found in the inner lining of
explanation: Squamous epithelial cells are found in the inner lining of the oesophagus. Simple squamous epithelium is a single layer of flat scale-shaped cells, which are helpful in transportation of food from buccal cavity to stomach.
subject: Biology

question_text: Transformation of meristematic cells into specific permanent tissues occurs by the process of
explanation: Transformation of meristematic cells into specific permanent tissues occurs by the process of cell differentiation. In this process, cells formed by meristematic tissues take up a specific role and lose the ability to divide. As a result, they form a permanent tissue taking up a permanent shape, size and function.
subject: Biology

question_text: The gaseous product of a process in plants is a requirement for another vital process that releases energy. Given below are four combinations of the process and product. Identify the correct answer.
explanation: In plants, oxygen gas is produced as by-product of photosynthesis which is required by aerobic cellular respiration to produce energy (ATP). Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplast while aerobic cellular respiration occurs in mitochondria.
subject: Biology

question_text: In a dicot pot herb, vaseline/vegetable oil was applied on the upper surface of one leaf (experimental leaf 1) and on the lower surface of another leaf (experimental leaf 2). Vaseline/Vegetable oil was not applied on the control leaf. The plant was deliberately not watered for several days. Which leaf will dry up last?
options: All the leaves will dry up simultaneously
explanation: Experimental leaf 2 will dry up last, because in dicot plants, stomata are generally found in lower surface of leaves and applying vaseline/vegetable oil will close these stomata, thus preventing the water loss through transpiration (evaporation of water in the form of vapour form leaf surface) and drying process will take a lot more time compare to other leaves.
subject: Biology

question_text: Which one of the following statements is not correct for light rays?
options: Light travels at different speeds in different media.
Light travel at almost 300 million metres per second in air.
Light speeds down as it leaves a water surface and enters the air.
Light speeds up as it leaves a glass surface and enters the air.
correct_answer: Light speeds down as it leaves a water surface and enters the air.
explanation: The speed of light in air is 3 x 10^8 m/s and the speed of light is different in different media.
subject: Physics

question_text: A glass prism splits white light into different colours. This phenomenon is called dispersion of light by prism. Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Red light will deviate the most and it is because of the reflection of light.
Violet light will deviate the most and it is because of the refraction of light.
Red light will deviate the most and it is because of the refraction of light.
Violet light will deviate the most and it is because of the reflection of light.
correct_answer: Violet light will deviate the most and it is because of the refraction of light.
explanation: VIBGYOR (increasing order of wavelength). (Frequency decreases in increasing order). Refractive index is inversely proportional to wavelength. So, violet light will deviate the most.
subject: Physics

question_text: A current of 1.0 A is drawn by a filament of an electric bulb for 10 minutes. The amount of electric charge that flows through the circuit is
explanation: Given, I = 1A, t = 10 min = 10 x 60 s = 600 s. I = Q/t => Q = It => Q = 1 x 600 => Q = 600 C
subject: Physics

question_text: Which one of the following formulae does not represent electrical power?
explanation: Electric power is the rate per unit time at which electrical energy is transferred by an electric circuit, P = I^2R = V^2/R = VI. Its SI unit is watt.
subject: Physics

question_text: The sound created in a big hall persists because of the repeated reflections. The phenomenon is called
explanation: The sound created in a big hall persists because of the repeated reflection. The phenomenon is called reverberation.
subject: Physics

question_text: When light is scattered by a molecule and the frequency of the scattered light is changed, this phenomenon is called
explanation: When light is scattered by a molecule and the frequency of the scattered light is changed, this phenomenon is called Raman effect.
subject: Physics

question_text: Which one of the following statements about the cleansing action of soap is not true?
options: (a) The oil and dirt gets collected in the centre of the micelle.
(c) Soaps are ammonium salts of long chain carboxylic acids.
(d) Soap forms insoluble precipitates with the calcium and magnesium ions in hard water.
explanation: Detergents are ammonium or sulphonate salts of long chain carboxylic acids. Hence, option (c) is not true. Soap is a mixture of sodium salts of various naturally occurring fatty acids.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Hydrogenation of vegetable oils using nickel catalyst is an example of
explanation: Hydrogenation of vegetable oils using nickel catalyst is an example of addition reaction. Hydrogenation is a process that uses hydrogen gas to change a liquid vegetable oil into a hard spread. This process stabilises the oil and prevents spoilage from oxidation.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Which one of the following materials is not an allotrope of carbon?
explanation: Diamond, graphene and fullerene are three allotropes of pure carbon. Fly ash is not an allotrope of carbon.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Which one of the following reactions does not result in the evolution of hydrogen gas?
options: (a) Reaction of zinc metal with dilute sulphuric acid solution
(b) Mixing water to Plaster of Paris
(c) Heating zinc metal with sodium hydroxide solution
(d) Reaction of potassium metal with water
explanation: When plaster of Paris is mixed with water, it gets converted into gypsum. i.e. CaSO4.1/2H2O + 1 1/2H2O -> CaSO4.2H2O. Hence, it doesn't give hydrogen gas.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Which one of the following acids is predominantly found in tomatoes?
explanation: Oxalic acid is a chemical compound that occur naturally in almost every plant to some degree including fruits, vegetables and grain plants. The amount of oxalic in tomatoes is about 50 mg per 100 g.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Which one of the following conclusions could not be derived from Rutherford’s alpha-particle scattering experiment?
options: (a) Most of the space in the atom is empty.
(b) The radius of the atom is about 10^5 times the radius of the nucleus.
(c) Electrons move in a circular path of fixed energy called orbits
(d) Nearly all the mass of the atom resides in the nucleus.
explanation: The concept of electrons move in a circular path of fixed energy called orbits was put forward by Bohr and not derived from Rutherford’s scattering experiment. Therefore, option (c) is incorrect.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Reaction of quick lime (CaO) with water to produce slaked lime (Ca(OH)2) is an example of
explanation: The formation of slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) Ca(OH)2 when water is added to lime (CaO) is exothermic. CaO(s) + H2O(l) -> Ca(OH)2(s) [Evolution of heat]
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Which one of the following is not a bio-mass energy source?
explanation: Nuclear reactors are sources of nuclear energy, not bio-mass energy. Wood, gobar gas and coal are the organic or bio-mass sources of energy.
subject: Physics

question_text: Twinkling of stars is due to
options: (b) reflection of starlight from the oceanic surface.
explanation: The twinkling of a star is due to atmospheric refraction of starlight. The starlight on entering the earth's atmosphere, undergoes refraction continuously before it reaches the earth. The atmospheric refraction occurs in the medium of gradually changing refractive index.
subject: Physics

question_text: Which one of the following cannot be the unit of frequency of a sound wave?
explanation: We know that, Frequency = 1 / Time period = 1 / Second or minute. Apart from this, the SI unit of frequency is hertz (Hz).
subject: Physics

question_text: ‘Beats’ is a phenomenon that occurs when frequencies of two harmonic waves are
explanation: When two sound waves of approximately equal frequency are produced simultaneously, the intensity of the resultant sound wave increases or decreases with time. This change in the intensity of sound is called beats.
subject: Physics

question_text: Light waves are incident on an air-glass boundary. Some of the light waves are reflected and some are refracted in the glass. Which one of the following properties is the same for the incident wave and the refracted wave?
explanation: Frequency of refracted and reflected wave never changes because the frequency does not depends on the medium.
subject: Physics

question_text: Which one of the following statements is true for a simple harmonic oscillator?
options: (a) Force acting is directly proportional to the displacement from the mean position and is in same direction.
(b) Force acting is directly proportional to the displacement from the mean position and is in opposite direction.
(c) Acceleration of the oscillator is constant.
(d) The velocity of the oscillator is not periodic.
explanation: F = -k x (SHM equation) where, x = displacement from mean position and F = acting force.
subject: Physics

question_text: During seed germination, the part of the embryo which grows into root is
explanation: During seed germination, the part of the embryo which grows into root is called radicle. It is the first part of a seedling (a growing plant embryo) to emerge from the seed during the process of germination to form embryonic root of the plant which grows downward in the soil.
subject: Biology

question_text: In a typical flower, germinating pollen grains pass through several parts of the gynoecium before they reach the ovule. A list of the parts of gynoecium is given below in different combinations. Choose the combination that represents the correct sequence of pollen tube pathway/journey.
explanation: Pollen grains gather on the surface of stigma of gynoecium through pollination and get germinated to produce pollen tube. This pollen tube elongated in style and reaches ovary to release male gametes in embryo sac of ovule.
subject: Biology

question_text: If human blood is placed in a 2% detergent solution, what will happen to the RBC?
options: (b) The RBC will swell and become turgid.
(c) The RBC will swell and burst.
explanation: If human blood is placed in a 2% detergent solution, the RBC will shrink. Detergent solution is a hypertonic solution compared to red blood cells, hence RBCs are, if placed in it, the cell will shrink due to exosmosis, i.e. movement of water from its higher concentration (RBC) to lower concentration (Detergent solution) through cell membrane (SPM) of RBCs.
subject: Biology

question_text: The major source of vitamins and minerals for vegetarians is
explanation: Vegetables and fruits are major source of vitamins and minerals for vegetarians.
subject: Biology

question_text: If a ray of light enters from a rarer medium to a denser medium at zero angle of incidence, it would
explanation: When light falls normally on the interface of two medium, then light travels in straight line. So, the refraction angle is zero.
subject: Physics

question_text: Mirage is an illustration of
options: (c) only total internal reflection of light
(d) both refraction and total internal reflection of light
explanation: A mirage is a naturally occurring optical phenomenon in which light rays bend via refraction to produce a displaced image of distant objects or the sky.
subject: Physics

question_text: Common salt (NaCl) is not used as a raw material for preparation of which one of the following compounds?
explanation: Preparation of plaster of Paris doesn't require the use of NaCl. It is simply obtained by heating gypsum (CaSO4 · 2H2O) at 120°C in a rotary kiln.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Which one of the following Harappan sites was a specialised centre for making shell object?
explanation: Among the given options, Harappan sites specialised centre for making shell object is Balakot and the other site is Nageshwar. Shell objects like bangles, ladles and inlay were made at these specialised centres.
subject: History

question_text: Which one of the following was not a part of the dhamma of King Ashoka?
options: (b) Tolerance of religions other than one's own
(d) Promoting the welfare of his subjects
explanation: Honouring the king was not a part of the Dhamma of king Ashoka. Dhamma of king Ashoka established the idea of paternal kingship. He regarded all his subjects as his children and believed it the king's duty to look after the welfare of the subjects. Ashoka's philosophy state that everybody should serve parents, revere teachers, and practice ahimsa and truthfulness. He asked everyone to avoid animal slaughter and sacrifice. He advocated tolerance towards all religions and sought conquest through Dhamma and not war.
subject: History

question_text:
Which of the following statements about Saguna Bhakti traditions is/are correct?
1. Saguna Bhakti traditions focus on the worship of specific deities such as Vishnu or his avatars.
2. In Saguna Bhakti traditions, Gods and Goddesses are conceptualised in anthropomorphic forms.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
explanation: Both the statements about Saguna Bhakti are correct. Saguna Bhakti has form, attributes and quality. Saguna saints worshipped the anthropomorphic manifestations of the divine being, particularly Vishnu or his avatars.
subject: History

question_text: At which one of the following places was a Shiva temple not constructed under the patronage of the Chola rulers?
explanation: Shiva Temple was not constructed at Naneghat under the patronage of the Chola rulers. Naneghat, is a mountain pass in the Western Ghats range between the Konkan coast and the ancient town of Junnar in the Deccan plateau. Chola empire was not extended to this region therefore no temple was build in the region.
subject: History

question_text: Which of the following statements about the Deccan Riots Commission is/are correct? 1. The Commission did not hold enquiries in the district which were not affected. 2. The Commission did record statements of ryots, sahukars eye-witnesses.
explanation: In 1875, peasants of Maharashtra in some parts of Pune and Ahmednagar districts revolted against increasing agrarian distress. The Deccan Riots of 1875 targeted conditions of debt peonage (kamiuti) to moneylenders. The rioters' specific purpose was to obtain and destroy the bonds, decrees, and other documents in the possession of the moneylenders. The movement also got support from the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha co-founded by M G Ranade. However, the Government of India pressurised Bombay to enquire into the matter for this the Deccan Riots Commission was set up which presented a report to the British Parliament in 1878. The commission did'nt hold inquiries in areas unaffected by it and also did'nt recorded the statements of royats, sahukars and eye-witnesses.
subject: History

question_text: Which one of the following is the correct meaning of ziyarat?
options: (a) Pilgrimage to the tombs of sufi saints.
(c) The death anniversary of a sufi Shaikh
correct_answer: (a) Pilgrimage to the tombs of sufi saints.
explanation: In Islam, ziyara or ziyarat is a form of pilgrimage to sites associated with Muhammad, his family members and descendants, his companions and other venerated figures in Islam such as the prophets, Sufi auliya, and Islamic scholars.
subject: History

question_text: Keppel Island is completely bleached mainly due to the expansion of
explanation: Keppel Island is completely bleached mainly due to the expansion of starfish. The population of starfish is growing unconditionally due to which starfish are able to eat coral; a polyp that builds limestone reef on which the coral community lives. Keppel Island is located in the southern Great Barrier reef. Coral bleaching is the process when corals become white due to various stressors, such as changes in temperature, light or nutrients.
subject: Geography

question_text: Which one of the following rivers is not a tributary of river Brahmaputra?
explanation: Among the given options, Mahananda river is not a tributary of river Brahmaputra. Tributaries of Brahmaputra: left-Lhasa River, Nyang River, Parlung Zangbo, Lohit River, Dhansiri River, Kolong River/ right-Kameng River, Manas River, Beki River, Raidak River, Jaldhaka River, Teesta River, Subansiri River. The Mahananda River is a trans-boundary river that flows through the states of Bihar and West Bengal, and Bangladesh. It is an important tributary of the Ganges.
subject: Geography

question_text: Which one of the following is not a minor plate?
explanation: Antarctic plate is not a minor plate. There are 15 minor plates, these smaller plates are often not shown on major plate maps. For purposes of this list, a minor plate is any plate with an area less than 20 million km^2 but greater than 1 million km^2. They are Somali Plate, Nazca Plate, Indian Plate, Amurian Plate, Sunda Plate, Philippine Sea Plate, Okhotsk Plate, Arabian Plate, Yangtze Plate, Caribbean Plate, Cocos Plate, Caroline Plate, Scotia Plate, Burma Plate, New Hebrides Plate.
subject: Geography

question_text: Advantage(s) of tectonic activity in Iceland include(s) 1. Source of natural geothermal energy 2. Creation of new land 3. Attraction of tourists
explanation: The tectonic plates whose turbulent interactions formed Iceland, are the Eurasian tectonic plate and the North American tectonic plate. Spanning the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, Iceland emerged as a result of the divergent, spreading, boundary between these two plates and the activity of Iceland's own hotspot or mantle plume.
subject: Geography

question_text: The process whereby certain minerals absorb water, expand and change is called as
explanation: The process whereby certain minerals absorb water, expand and change is called as Hydration. A good example of hydration is the absorption of water by anhydrite, resulting in the formation of gypsum. Hydration expands volume and also results in rock deformation.
subject: Geography

question_text: Which one of the following is the longest Latitude?
explanation: The longest latitude is 0 degree latitude, known as the Equator which divides the Earth into two equal halves, the northern hemisphere and two southern hemisphere.
subject: Geography

question_text: If it is 12:00 Noon in India, on which meridian will it be 7:00 am of the same day?
explanation: If it is 12:00 Noon in India, on 75 degree, W. Longitude it will be 7:00 am of the same day. Current time in India = 12:00 PM. Time at required meridian = 7:00 AM. Difference in time = 5 Hours, and this time at meridian (7:00 AM) is 5 hours behind. Hence, it is west direction. As we know the Earth takes 24 hours, for one complete rotation, so 24 hours = 360 degree. 1 hour = 360/24 = 15 degree, thus the Earth rotates 15 degree in/hour. In 5 hours = 5 x 15 = 75 degree. Hence, at 75 degree West longitude, the time will be 7:00 AM.
subject: Geography

question_text: Who among the following was considered to be the preceptor of Mirabai?
explanation: Guru Raidas, a low caste leather worker was the preceptor of Mirabai. He was low class leather worker. One of the main principle of her philosophy was that one should abandon the comforts of life and devote fully to her God for attainment of peace and salvation.
subject: History

question_text: Consider the following statements about the Mahanavami Dibba: 1. It was the name of a giant box of sweets distributed at the Mahanavami festival. 2. It was the name of a massive platform with a base covered with relief carvings. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Mahanavami Dibba was the name of massive platform with a base covered with relief carvings was the King's palace in Vijayanagara though there is no definite evidence. The Mahanavami Dibba had a very impressive platform known as 'the audience hall'. It was surrounded by high double walls a street running between them.
subject: History

question_text: Which one of the following statements about the Ain-i-Akbari is not correct?
options: It was written by Abu'l Fazl.
It is a part of a larger work called Akbar Nama.
It describes the Mughal Empire as having a diverse population and a composite culture.
It was later revised by Sadullah Khan on the orders of Shah Jahan.
correct_answer: It was later revised by Sadullah Khan on the orders of Shah Jahan.
explanation: Abu'l Fazl worked on the 'Akbar Nama'. The Akbar Nama is divided into three books: The first book dealt with Akbar's ancestors, the second recorded the events of Akbar's reign, the third is the Ain-i Akbari. Badshah Nama was written by Abul Hamid Lahori was later revised by Sadullah Khan on the orders of Shah Jahan.
subject: History

question_text: Swami Dayanand Saraswati 1. was opposed to the worship of idols of Gods and Goddesses. 2. regarded the Vedas as infallible. 3. had met and had discussions with Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: All the statements are correct. Swami Dayanand Saraswati was a philosopher, social leader and founder of Arya Samaj. He was opposed to the worship of idols of Gods and Goddesses as he believe that God has no shape and no form. Hence, statement 1 is correct. Swami Dayanand regarded vedas as eternal and infallible. Hence, statement 2 is correct. He met Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar in Calcutta and had discussions with him. Hence, statement 3 is correct.
subject: History

question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Muhammad Anglo-Oriental College was founded in Aligarh by Sayyid Ahmad Khan. 2. Sayyid Ahmad Khan was a great believer in religious toleration, and Hindus, Paris and Christians had contributed to the funds of his college. Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
explanation: Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College was founded in 1875 by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, initially as a primary school, with the intention of taking it to a college level institution, known as Muhammadan Anglo Collegiate School. Sayyid Ahmad Khan was a great believer in religious toleration. He believed that all religions had a certain underlying unity which could be called practical morality. Hindus, Parsis, and Christians had contributed freely to the funds of his college whose doors were open for all the Indians.
subject: History

question_text: Basket-of-eggs topography is related to
explanation: Basket of eggs topography is related to Drumlins. Drumlins which is a depositional landform formed by glaciers. They are forms of rounded hummocks resulting from the deposition of glacial till which look like inverted boat or spoon.
subject: Geography

question_text: Which one of the following planets has the highest density?
explanation: Among the given options, Earth has the highest density. Earth is the fourth smallest of the planets. Earth is the densest planet because it is made of dense material and it is heavy planet. The Average Density of Earth is 5.5 grams/cm^3.
subject: Geography

question_text: Point of Origin of Earthquake wave is known as
explanation: The focus is the place inside Earth's crust where an earthquake originates. The point on the Earth's surface directly above the focus is the epicentre.
subject: Geography

question_text: The maximum depth of Lithosphere is found in the
explanation: The maximum depth lithosphere is found in the pacific ocean. Earth's lithosphere, which constitutes the hard and rigid outer vertical layer of the Earth, includes the crust and the uppermost mantle. Mariana Trench is located in the western Pacific Ocean, it is the deepest oceanic trench on Earth and the deepest part of the Earth.
subject: Geography

question_text: A large body of magmatic material that cools in the deeper depth of the Earth's crust and develops in the form of large domes is known as
explanation: A large body of magmatic material that cools in the deeper depth of the Earth's crust and develops in the form of large domes is known as Batholiths. Forms from cooled magma deep in Earth's crust. These areas are exposed to the surface through the process of erosion accelerated by continental uplift acting over many tens of millions to hundreds of millions of years.
subject: Geography

question_text: Which one of the following Oil Refineries is not located in Assam?
explanation: Among the given options, Tatipaka Oil Refinery is not located in Assam, it is located in Andhra Pradesh. It was established in 2001. It is ONGC's first ever oil refinery to produce petro-products.
subject: Geography

question_text: Where and when did Mahatma Gandhi make his first public appearance in India on coming back from South Africa after two decades?
explanation: Gandhi's first public appearance in India was on the occasion of the opening ceremony of the Banaras Hindu University in February 1916, which was distinguished by the presence of many magnets and princes and of the Viceroy himself. He also passed critical comments on the Princes, as a result many princes walked out.
subject: History

question_text: When and where was the demand for 'Purna Swaraj' or complete independence made by the Indian National Congress?
explanation: The Indian National Congress, on 19th December, 1929, passed the 'Purna Swaraj' - (total independence) resolution - at its Lahore session. A public declaration was made on 26th January, 1930 - a day which the Congress Party urged Indians to celebrate as 'Independence Day'. The declaration was passed due to the breakdown of negotiations between leaders of the freedom movement and the British over the question of dominion status for India.
subject: History

question_text: Which one of the following provides for the complete equality of men and women in India?
options: (a) Articles 14 and 15 of the Constitution of India
(b) Fifth Schedule of the Constitution of India
(d) Article 20 of the Constitution of India
explanation: Article 14: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. Article 15 secures the citizens from every sort of discrimination by the State, on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth or any of them. However, this Article does not prevent the State from making any special provisions for women or children.
subject: Indian Polity

question_text: Which of the following statements about the non-permanent member of the Security Council of the United Nation is/are correct? 1. Their total number is now 10 but was originally only 6. 2. They are elected for a term of two years only. Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
explanation: The UNSC is composed of 15 members, 5 permanent and 10 non-permanent. Five permanent members: China, France, the Russian Federation, the United Kingdom, and the United States and Ten non-permanent members: Elected for two-year terms by the General Assembly. Each year, the General Assembly elects five non-permanent members (out of ten in total) for a two-year term. The ten non-permanent seats are distributed on a regional basis. As stipulated in rule 144 of the rules of procedure, a retiring member is not eligible for immediate re-election.
subject: International Relations

question_text: At which of the following was the American Declaration of Independence adopted on 4th July, 1776?
explanation: The United States Declaration of Independence is the pronouncement adopted by the Second Continental Congress meeting in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, on 4th July, 1776.
subject: History

question_text: Who among the following was the head of the Government that was overthrown by the Bolsheviks in the 1917 Revolution?
explanation: Tsar Nicolas II was the head of the Government that was overthrown by the Bolsheviks in the 1917 Revolution. The Russian Revolution was a period of political and social revolution that took place in the former Russian Empire and began during the First World War. The Russian Revolution was a series of two revolutions: the first of which overthrew the imperial government and the second placed the Bolsheviks in power. That Caused the Tsar of the Russian Empire, Nicholas II, to step down from his throne.
subject: History

question_text: Which one of the following is not a form of non-permanent member of the Security condensation?
explanation: Condensation is the change of the state of matter from the gas phase into the liquid phase, and is the reverse of vaporisation. The word most often refers to the water cycle. Sleet is Rain and snow mixed is precipitation composed of rain and partially melted snow.
subject: Geography

question_text: Which one of the following clouds is a rain-bearing cloud?
explanation: Nimbus cloud is a rain-bearing cloud. Nimbus clouds are dark clouds as they carry a substantial quantity of water droplets. Nimbus comes in union with other cloud forms that bring substantial precipitation.
subject: Geography

question_text: In which one of the following countries is intensive subsistence agriculture not predominantly practised?
explanation: N/A
subject: Geography

question_text: The Headquarters of South-Eastern Railway is located at
explanation: The Headquarters of South-Eastern Railway is located at Kolkata (Gardern Reach). It is the administrative and purchase office of the entire zone.
subject: Geography

question_text: Bharatmala Pariyojana is related to
options: (a) interlinking of Northern and Southern Indian rivers in a garland shape.
(b) networks of National Highways in India.
(c) interlinking of all cities of India through Railways.
(d) interlinking of all industrial regions of India through pipelines.
correct_answer: (b) networks of National Highways in India.
explanation: Bharatmala Pariyojana is an umbrella program for the highways sector envisaged by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. To optimise the efficiency of freight and passenger movement across the country by bridging critical infrastructure gaps through effective interventions.
subject: Geography

question_text: The natural vegetation which covers maximum geographical areas of India is
explanation: Tropical deciduous are a variety of temperate forest 'dominated' by trees that lose their leaves each year. They are found in areas with warm moist summers and cold winters.
subject: Geography

question_text: River Beas, flowing from Himachal Punjab, joins the river
explanation: River Beas, flowing from Himachal, Punjab, joint the river Settuj. The Beas River rises in the Himalayas in central Himachal Pradesh, and flows for some 470 km to the Setluj River in the Indian state of Punjab.
subject: Geography

question_text: Which one of the following is not a power of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha ?
options: (a) Speaker shall preside over the House of the People.

question_text: If matrix A = [[1-i, i], [-i, 1-i]] where i = sqrt(-1), then which one of the following is correct?

Now, consider X = (conjugate A)^T + A = [[1+i, i], [-i, 1+i]] + [[1-i, i], [-i, 1-i]] = [[2, 2i], [-2i, 2]]. Conjugate X = [[2, -2i], [2i, 2]]. (Conjugate X)^T = [[2, 2i], [-2i, 2]] = X. Hence, (conjugate A)^T + A is a hermitian matrix.

question_text: If tan θ = (cos 17° - sin 17°) / (cos 17° + sin 17°), then what is the value of θ?

question_text: A and B are positive acute angles such that cos 2B = 3 sin^2 A and 3 sin 2A = 2 sin 2B. What is the value of (A + 2B)?

question_text: What is sin 3x + cos 3x + 4 sin^3 x - 3 sin x + 3 cos x - 4 cos^3 x equal to?

question_text: What is the value of 8 cos 10° cos 20° cos 40°?

question_text: What is the value of cos 48° - cos 12°?

question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. If ABC is a right-angled triangle, right-angled at A and if sin B = 1/3, then cosec C = 3. 2. If b cos B = c cos C and if the triangle ABC is not right-angled, then ABC must be isosceles. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
explanation: Statement 1: In right triangle ABC, sin B = AC/BC = 1/3. Then cosec C = BC/AB. Since AB = sqrt(BC^2 - AC^2) = sqrt(9k^2 - k^2) = sqrt(8)k, cosec C = 3/sqrt(8), which is not 3. Statement 2: b cos B = c cos C implies sin B cos B = sin C cos C, so sin 2B = sin 2C. This leads to 2B = 2C or 2B = 180 - 2C, implying B=C, so it is isosceles.

question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. If in a triangle ABC, A = 2B and b = c, then it must be an obtuse-angled triangle. 2. There exists no triangle ABC with A = 40°, B = 65° and a/c = sin 40° cosec 15°. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
explanation: For statement 1: In triangle ABC, A=2B and b=c implies angle C = angle B. Since A+B+C=180, 2B+B+B=180, 4B=180, B=45, C=45, A=90. It is a right-angled triangle, not obtuse. For statement 2: A=40, B=65, C=75. Using sine rule a/sin 40 = c/sin 75, so a/c = sin 40/sin 75 = sin 40 cosec 75. The statement says sin 40 cosec 15, which is incorrect.

question_text: What is tan^2 x equal to?

question_text: What is (d - a)/(b - d) equal to?

question_text: What is p^2/q^2 equal to?

question_text: What is (t3 - t5)/(t5 - t7) equal to?

question_text: If sin x + sin y = cos y - cos x, where 0 < y < x < pi/2, then what is tan((x-y)/2) equal to?

question_text: If p^2, q^2 and r^2 (where p, q, r > 0) are in GP, then which of the following is/are correct? 1. p, q and r in GP. 2. ln p, ln q and ln r are in AP.

question_text: If cot α and cot β are the roots of the equation x^2 - 3x + 2 = 0, then what is cot (α + β) equal to?

question_text: The roots α and β of a quadratic equation, satisfy the relations α + β = α^2 + β^2 and αβ = α^2β^2. What is the number of such quadratic equations?

question_text: What is the argument of the complex number (1 - i sqrt(3)) / (1 + i sqrt(3)), where i = sqrt(-1)?

question_text: What is the modulus of the complex number (cos theta + i sin theta) / (cos theta - i sin theta) where i = sqrt(-1)?

question_text: Let p, q and r be three distinct positive real numbers. If D = |p q r; q r p; r p q|, then which one of the following is correct?

question_text: What is the sum of the last five coefficients in the expansion of (1 + x)^9 when it is expanded in ascending powers of x?

question_text: The point (1, -1) is one of the vertices of a square. If 3x + 2y = 5 is the equation of one diagonal of the square, then what is the equation of the other diagonal?

question_text: Let P(x, y) be any point on the ellipse 25x^2 + 16y^2 = 400. If Q(0, 3) and R(0, -3) are two points, then what is (PQ + PR) equal to?
explanation: The ellipse is x^2/16 + y^2/25 = 1. Here a^2=16, b^2=25. Since b > a, foci are (0, +/- ae). e = sqrt(1 - 16/25) = 3/5. Foci are (0, +/- 3). Q and R are foci. By definition, sum of focal distances = 2b = 2*5 = 10.

question_text: If the circumcentre of the triangle formed by the lines x + 2 = 0, y + 2 = 0 and kx + y + 2 = 0 is (- 1, - 1), then what is the value of k?

question_text: In the parabola, y^2 = x, what is the length of the chord passing through the vertex and inclined to the X-axis at an angle θ?
explanation: For parabola y^2 = 4ax, here a = 1/4. Any point on the parabola is P(t^2, t). The line passing through the vertex (0,0) and inclined at angle θ has slope tan θ = y/x = t/t^2 = 1/t. Thus t = cot θ. The point P is (cot^2 θ, cot θ). The length of the chord is sqrt((cot^2 θ - 0)^2 + (cot θ - 0)^2) = sqrt(cot^4 θ + cot^2 θ) = cot θ * sqrt(cot^2 θ + 1) = cot θ * cosec θ = (cos θ / sin θ) * (1 / sin θ) = cos θ * cosec^2 θ.

question_text: Under which condition, are the points (a, b), (c, d) and (a - c, b - d) collinear?

question_text: Let ABC be a triangle. If D (2, 5) and E (5, 9) are the mid-points of the sides AB and AC respectively, then what is the length of the side BC?
explanation: The length of the segment DE is sqrt((5-2)^2 + (9-5)^2) = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = sqrt(9+16) = 5. By the Midpoint Theorem, the side BC is twice the length of the segment connecting the midpoints of the other two sides. Therefore, BC = 2 * DE = 2 * 5 = 10.

question_text: If the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point (0, k) to the line 3x - 4y - 5 = 0 is (3, 1), then what is the value of k?
explanation: The line passing through (0, k) and (3, 1) is perpendicular to 3x - 4y - 5 = 0. The slope of the given line is 3/4, so the slope of the perpendicular line is -4/3. Using the slope formula: (1 - k) / (3 - 0) = -4/3. 1 - k = -4, so k = 5.

question_text: If 3x - 4y - 5 = 0 and 3x - 4y + 15 = 0 are the equations of a pair of opposite sides of a square, then what is the area of the square?

question_text: What is the length of the diameter of the sphere whose centre is at (1, -2, 3) and which touches the plane 6x - 3y + 2z - 4 = 0?

question_text: What is the perpendicular distance from the point (2, 3, 4) to the line (x-0)/1 = (y-0)/0 = (z-0)/0?
explanation: Let the line be L. Any point on the line is Q(lambda, 0, 0). Vector PQ = (lambda-2, -3, -4). Since PQ is perpendicular to the line (direction 1, 0, 0), the dot product is (lambda-2)*1 + (-3)*0 + (-4)*0 = 0, so lambda = 2. Point Q is (2, 0, 0). Distance PQ = sqrt((2-2)^2 + (3-0)^2 + (4-0)^2) = sqrt(0 + 9 + 16) = 5 units.

question_text: If p(x) = (4e)^2x, then what is integral(p(x) dx) equal to?
explanation: We have p(x) = (4e)^2x. integral(p(x)dx) = integral((4e)^2x dx) = integral(4^2x * e^2x dx). By using integration by parts, we get integral(p(x)dx) = (4^2x * e^2x) / 2 - integral(4^2x * log(4) * 2 * e^2x / 2 dx) = (4^2x * e^2x) / 2 - log(4) * integral(p(x)dx). Thus, (1 + log 4) * integral(p(x)dx) = p(x) / 2. Therefore, integral(p(x)dx) = p(x) / (2(1 + log 4)) = p(x) / (2(1 + 2 log 2)).

The value of R is
explanation:
In the above circuit, both resistance of R R are connected in parallel combination.

question_text: If the roots of the equation a(b - c)x^2 + b(c - a)x + c(a - b) = 0 are equal, then which one of the following is correct?

question_text: Consider the following statements in respect of the quadratic equation 4(x - p)(x - q) - r^2 = 0, where p, q and r are real numbers. 1. The roots are real. 2. The roots are equal, if p = q and r = 0. Which of the above statements is/are correct?

question_text: If the angle between the lines joining the end points of minor axis of the ellipse x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1 with one of the foci is pi/2, then what is the eccentricity of the ellipse?

Then, the point (r + 4, r + 2, 2r + k) lies on the plane, we get 2(r + 4) - 4(r + 2) + (2r + k) = 7 => 2r + 8 - 4r - 8 + 2r + k = 7 => k = 7.

question_text: A straight line passes through the point (1, 1, 1) makes an angle 60 degree with the positive direction of Z-axis, and the cosine of the angles made by it with the positive directions of the Y-axis and the X-axis are in the ratio sqrt(3) : 1. What is the acute angle between the two possible positions of the line?
explanation: Let the straight line makes the angle with X-axis, Y-axis and Z-axis be alpha, beta and gamma. gamma = 60 degree and cos(beta)/cos(alpha) = sqrt(3)/1. If l, m and n are the direction cosines of the lines, then n = cos(gamma) = cos(60 degree) = 1/2. And m/l = cos(beta)/cos(alpha) = sqrt(3)/1 => m = sqrt(3)l = kl (Let). We know that, l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1. k^2 + 3k^2 + 1/4 = 1 => 4k^2 = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4 => k^2 = 3/16 => k = +/- sqrt(3)/4. l1 = -sqrt(3)/4, m1 = -3/4, n1 = 1/2 and l2 = sqrt(3)/4, m2 = -3/4, n2 = 1/2. We know that, cos(theta) = |l1l2 + m1m2 + n1n2| => cos(theta) = |-3/16 + 9/16 + 1/4| = |-3/16 + 9/16 + 4/16| = |10/16| = 5/8. question_text: What is the minimum value of a^2/cos^2(x) + b^2/sin^2(x) where a > 0 and b > 0?

question_text: If the angles of a triangle ABC are in AP and b:c = sqrt(3):sqrt(2), then what is the measure of angle A?

question_text: If tan A - tan B = x and cot B - cot A = y, then what is the value of cot(A - B)?
explanation: Given tan A - tan B = x and cot B - cot A = y. cot B - cot A = (1/tan B) - (1/tan A) = (tan A - tan B)/(tan A tan B) = x/(tan A tan B) = y. So tan A tan B = x/y. cot(A - B) = (cot A cot B + 1)/(cot B - cot A) = (1/(tan A tan B) + 1)/y = (y/x + 1)/y = 1/x + 1/y.

explanation: Using the property integral(0 to a) f(x) dx = integral(0 to a) f(a-x) dx, I1 = π * integral(0 to π) dx / (1 + sin x) = π * [tan x - sec x] from 0 to π = π.
subject: Mathematics

question_text: What is the value of I1 + I2?
explanation: I1 = π, I2 = 0 (by symmetry of the integral). Thus I1 + I2 = π.
subject: Mathematics

question_text: The differential equation which represents the family of curves given by tan y = C(1 - e^x) is
options: e^x tan y dx + (1 - e^x) dy = 0
e^x tan y dx + (1 - e^x) sec^2 y dy = 0
e^x (1 - e^x) dx + tan y dy = 0
e^x tan y dy + (1 - e^x) sec^2 y dy = 0
explanation: The equation of the family of curves is tan y = C(1 - e^x). Differentiating w.r.t. x, we get sec^2 y (dy/dx) = -C e^x. Eliminating C, we get sec^2 y (dy/dx) = -e^x (tan y / (1 - e^x)). Rearranging gives e^x tan y dx + (1 - e^x) sec^2 y dy = 0.
subject: Mathematics

question_text: What is the derivative of 2^(sin x)^2 with respect to sin x?
explanation: Derivative of 2^(sin x)^2 with respect to sin x is (d/d(sin x)) [2^(sin x)^2] = 2^(sin x)^2 * ln 2 * (d/d(sin x)) (sin x)^2 = 2^(sin x)^2 * ln 2 * 2 sin x = sin x * 2^(sin x)^2 * 2 ln 2 = sin x * 2^(sin x)^2 * ln 4.
subject: Mathematics

question_text: For what value of k is the function f(x) = {2x + 1/4, x < 0; k, x = 0; (x + 1/2)^2, x > 0} continuous?
explanation: For continuity at x=0, LHL = RHL = f(0). LHL = lim(x->0-) (2x + 1/4) = 1/4. RHL = lim(x->0+) (x + 1/2)^2 = 1/4. Since f(0) = k, k must be 1/4.
subject: Mathematics

question_text: What is the area of the region enclosed between the curve y^2 = 2x and the straight line y = x?
explanation: Intersection points: y^2 = 2y => y=0, 2. Area = integral from 0 to 2 of (y - y^2/2) dy = [y^2/2 - y^3/6] from 0 to 2 = (4/2 - 8/6) = 2 - 4/3 = 2/3.
subject: Mathematics

question_text: If f(x) = x^3/3 - 5x^2/2 + 6x + 7 increases in the interval T and decreases in the interval S, then which one of the following is correct?
explanation: f'(x) = x^2 - 5x + 6 = (x-2)(x-3). f'(x) > 0 (increasing) when x < 2 or x > 3. f'(x) < 0 (decreasing) when 2 < x < 3.

question_text: A bag contains 20 books out of which 5 are defective. If 3 of the books are selected at random and removed from the bag in succession without replacement, then what is the probability that all three books are defective?
explanation: Total books in bag = 20. Defective books = 5. Probability of selecting three defective books without replacement = (5/20) * (4/19) * (3/18) = 6/684 = 0.0087 = 0.009.
subject: Mathematics

question_text: The median of the observations 22, 24, 33, 37, x + 1, x + 3, 46, 47, 57, 58 in ascending order is 42. What are the values of 5th and 6th observations respectively?
explanation: For 10 observations, median is the average of 5th and 6th terms. (x+1 + x+3)/2 = 42 => 2x + 4 = 84 => 2x = 80 => x = 40. 5th observation = x+1 = 41, 6th observation = x+3 = 43.
subject: Mathematics

question_text: Arithmetic mean of 10 observations is 60 and sum of squares of deviations from 50 is 5000. What is the standard deviation of the observations?
explanation: Mean = 60, n = 10. Sum of observations = 600. Sum of squares of deviations from 50 = 5000. SD = sqrt(sum(di^2)/n - (sum(di)/n)^2) where di = xi - 50. Sum(di) = Sum(xi) - 50*10 = 600 - 500 = 100. SD = sqrt(5000/10 - (100/10)^2) = sqrt(500 - 100) = sqrt(400) = 20.
subject: Mathematics

question_text: For the variables x and y, the two regression lines are 6x + y = 30 and 3x + 2y = 25. What are the values of x_bar, y_bar and r respectively?
explanation: Solving 6x+y=30 and 3x+2y=25 gives x=35/9 and y=20/3. Regression lines are 6x+y=30 (y = -6x + 30, slope b_yx = -6) and 3x+2y=25 (x = -2/3y + 25/3, slope b_xy = -2/3). r^2 = b_yx * b_xy = (-6) * (-2/3) = 4. Since slopes are negative, r = -sqrt(4) = -2 (Note: The provided solution in the image indicates r = -0.5, which contradicts the standard calculation for these specific lines).

question_text: The class marks in a frequency table are given to be 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50. The class limits of the first five classes are
explanation: Class interval = 10-5 = 5. Lower limit L1 = Class mark - interval/2 = 5 - 2.5 = 2.5. Upper limit L2 = Class mark + interval/2 = 5 + 2.5 = 7.5. First class is 2.5-7.5.

question_text: Two dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers appearing on them is a prime number?

question_text: If 5 of a Company's 10 delivery trucks do not meet emission standards and 3 of them are chosen for inspection, then what is the probability that none of the trucks chosen will meet emission standards?

question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. If A and B are mutually exclusive events, then it is possible that P(A) = P(B) = 0.6. 2. If A and B are any two events such that P(A/B) = 1, then P(B/A) = 1. Which of the above statement is/are correct?
explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect as P(A)+P(B) > 1. Statement 2 is correct as P(A/B)=1 implies B is a subset of A, and P(B/A) = P(A intersection B)/P(A) = P(B)/P(A) = 1.
subject: Mathematics

question_text: If a fair die is rolled 4 times, then what is the probability that there are exactly 2 sixes?
explanation: Let X be a random variable that represents to appearing 6 of rolled a die. Probability of to get 6 to rolled a die, p = 1/6. Probability of not get 6 to rolled a die, q = 1 - 1/6 = 5/6. Here, n = 4, r = 2. Required probability = nCr * p^r * q^(n-r) = 4C2 * (1/6)^2 * (5/6)^2 = 6 * (1/36) * (25/36) = 25/216.
subject: Mathematics

question_text: Mean of 100 observations is 50 and standard deviation is 10. If 5 is added to each observation, then what will be the new mean and new standard deviation respectively?
explanation: Mean of 100 observations = 50 and standard deviation = 10. If k is added to each observation, then new mean will be more than k and standard deviation no change. After 5 added to each observation, mean = 50 + 5 = 55 and standard deviation = 10.

question_text: If the range of a set of observations on a variable X is known to be 25 and if Y = 40 + 3X, then what is the range of the set of corresponding observations on Y?
explanation: Range of X = 25. Range = Xmax - Xmin. Given Y = 40 + 3X. Ymax = 40 + 3Xmax, Ymin = 40 + 3Xmin. Range of Y = Ymax - Ymin = (40 + 3Xmax) - (40 + 3Xmin) = 3(Xmax - Xmin) = 3 * 25 = 75.

question_text: A car travels first 60 km at a speed of 3v km/h and travels next 60 km at 2v km/h. What is the average speed of the car?
explanation: Average speed = Total distance / Total time. Total distance = 60 + 60 = 120 km. Total time = (60/3v) + (60/2v) = 20/v + 30/v = 50/v. Average speed = 120 / (50/v) = 120v / 50 = 2.4v km/h.

question_text: The mean weight of 150 students in a certain class is 60 kg. The mean weight of boys is 70 kg and that of girls is 55 kg. What are the number of boys and girls respectively in the class?
explanation: Let number of boys be x and girls be y. x + y = 150. Total weight = 150 * 60 = 9000. 70x + 55y = 9000. Dividing by 5: 14x + 11y = 1800. Substitute y = 150 - x: 14x + 11(150 - x) = 1800 => 14x + 1650 - 11x = 1800 => 3x = 150 => x = 50. y = 100.

question_text: A thin disc and a thin ring, both have mass M and radius R. Both rotate about axes through their centre of mass and are perpendicular to their surfaces at the same angular velocity. Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: (a) The ring has higher kinetic energy.
(b) The disc has higher kinetic energy.
(c) The ring and the disc both have the same kinetic energy.
(d) Kinetic energies of both the bodies are zero, since they are not in linear motion.
explanation: Given, a thin disc and a thin ring have equal mass and radius. Angular velocity of thin disc = Angular velocity of thin ring. w_ring = w_disc. Kinetic energy of ring = 1/2 * I_ring * w_ring^2 = 1/2 * (MR^2) * w_ring^2. Kinetic energy of disc = 1/2 * I_disc * w_disc^2 = 1/2 * (1/2 * MR^2) * w_disc^2. Since I_ring > I_disc, KE_ring > KE_disc.

options: (c) Both have the same moment of inertia
(d) The information provided is not sufficient to answer the question
explanation: As we know, moment of the inertia I_disc = 1/2 MR^2 and I_sphere = 2/5 MR^2. Given, M_disc = M_sphere and R_disc = R_sphere. So, I_disc / I_sphere = (1/2) / (2/5) = 5/4. Hence, from Eq. (i), I_disc > I_sphere. So, the disc has higher moment of inertia.
subject: Physics

question_text: Two substances of densities rho1 and rho2 are mixed in equal volume and their relative density is 4. When they are mixed in equal masses, relative density is 3. The values of rho1 and rho2 respectively, are
explanation: When substances are mixed in equal volume, relative density = (rho1 + rho2) / 2 = 4 => rho1 + rho2 = 8. Similarly, when substances are mixed in equal mass, relative density = 2*rho1*rho2 / (rho1 + rho2) = 3. Substituting rho1 + rho2 = 8, we get 2*rho1*rho2 / 8 = 3 => rho1*rho2 = 12. Solving rho1 + rho2 = 8 and rho1*rho2 = 12, we get rho1 = 6 and rho2 = 2.
subject: Physics

question_text: A car starts from Bengaluru, goes 50 km in a straight line towards South, immediately turns around and returns to Bengaluru. The time taken for this round trip is 2h. The magnitude of the average velocity of the car for this round trip
options: (d) cannot be calculated without knowing acceleration
explanation: According to question, a round trip is mentioned by a car. But as we know, for round trip the displacement is zero. So, v_av = displacement / time = 0 / 2 = 0 ms^-1.
subject: Physics

question_text: "The sum of emf's and potential differences around a closed loop equals zero" is a consequence of
explanation: It is Kirchhoff's second law also known as loop's law. i.e. sum(E) = sum(iR). It is based on conservation of energy, since work done in a closed path is zero.
subject: Physics

question_text: A student measures certain lengths using a meter scale having least count equal to 1 mm. Which one of the following measurement is more precise?
explanation: Using instrument of higher precision improving experimental techniques, etc., we can reduce the least count error. Here, option (c) 0.925 mm is more precise than other.
subject: Physics

question_text: If the work done on the system or by the system is zero, then which one of the following statement for a gas kept at a certain temperature is correct?
options: (a) Change in internal energy of the system is equal to flow of the heat in or out of the system.
(b) Change in internal energy of the system is less than heat transferred.
(c) Change in internal energy of the system is more than the heat flow.
explanation: For first law of thermodynamics, ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW where, ΔQ = heat, ΔU = change in internal energy and ΔW = work done. Since, ΔW = 0 So, ΔQ = ΔU Hence, there is change in internal energy of the system is equal to flow of heat in or out of the system, option (a) is correct.
subject: Physics

question_text: The total electrical resistance in the given part of the electric circuit is (Diagram shows 2 ohm, 4 ohm, 8 ohm resistors in parallel, connected in series with a 1 ohm resistor)
explanation: There are three resistances (2 ohm, 4 ohm and 8 ohm) are in parallel. So, 1/R1 = 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 => R1 = 8/7 ohm. Now, R1 is in series with 1 ohm resistance. So, Req = 1 ohm + R1 = 1 + 8/7 = 15/7 ohm. Hence, option (b) is correct.
subject: Physics

question_text: Which one of the following statements regarding lenses is not correct?
options: (a) A convex lens produces both real and virtual images.
(b) A concave lens produces both real and virtual images.
(c) A convex lens can produce images equal, greater and smaller than the size of the object.
(d) A concave lens always produces images smaller than the size of the object.
explanation: A concave lens always forms virtual image, whereas convex lens forms both real and virtual images. Hence, option (b) is incorrect.
subject: Physics

question_text: 10 g of ice at -10 degree C is mixed with 10 g of water at 0 degree C. The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of mixture to 10 degree C is
explanation: Heat require by 10 g of water at -10 degree C to 0 degree C is H1 = msΔθ = 10 * (0.50) * (0 - (-10)) = 50 cal. Now, latent heat of melting of 10 g of ice H2 = mL = 10 * 80 = 800 cal. Now, there is 20 g of water at 0 degree C, so heat required to reach the temperature of + 10 degree C. H3 = msΔθ = 20 * 1 * (10 - 0) = 200 cal. Total heat required, H = H1 + H2 + H3 = 50 + 800 + 200 = 1050 cal
subject: Physics

question_text: Which one of the following does not represent the salt, calcium carbonate?
explanation: Calcium carbonate is also known as limestone and has a molecular formula is CaCO3. It is found in nature in the form of chalk, marble etc. Thus, limestone, chalk and marble represents calcium carbonate. Whereas, lime water is the aqueous solution of Ca(OH)2. Thus, the correct option is (a).
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Soaps clean surfaces on the principle of based on
explanation: Soaps clean surfaces on the principle of based on surface tension. Soap is a surface active agent or surfactant. It helps to reduce the surface tension of water and thereby speed up the cleaning process of soaps.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Which one of the following substances is not a mixture?
explanation: A mixture is a type of matter which has variable composition throughout. Among the given options, only Sn(tin) is not a mixture, while rest are the examples of mixture. Sn is an element which contains only one kind of particles or atoms.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Which one of the following is termed as 'dry ice'?
explanation: When liquefied CO2 is allowed to expand rapidly, it gets converted in the form of solid CO2 which is also called dry ice. Thus, dry ice is solid state of the carbon dioxide.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Net movement of water from a dilute to a concentrated solution through a selectively permeable membrane is called
explanation: The net movement of water from a dilute to concentrated solution through a selectively permeable membrane is called osmosis. This term is used specifically to refers to the diffusions of water across semi or selectively permeable membrane. Water moves from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration until an equilibrium is reached.
subject: Biology

question_text: Blood is a type of
explanation: Blood is a type of connective tissue, which forms 30-32% of total extracellular fluid. The connective tissues have a special function of linking and supporting other tissues/organs of the body. Blood is a fluid, which helps in the transportation of various substances in the body. It is red because it contains a red pigment called haemoglobin in its red blood cells.
subject: Biology

question_text: Mitochondria are able to produce their own
explanation: N/A
subject: Biology

question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Xylem consists of tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres
Flexibility in plants is due to sclerenchyma
Xylem consists of sieve plate, sieve tube and companion cells
explanation: The statement given in option (a) is correct. Rest of the statements are incorrect and can be corrected as: (b) Flexibility in plants is due to the permanent tissue collenchyma. Sclerenchyma provides mechanical support to organs. (c) Parenchyma cells are thin walled with small intercellular spaces. (d) Phloem consists of sieve plates, sieve tube and companion cells.
subject: Biology

question_text: Who among the following popularised the use of embryological characters in taxonomy?
explanation: Panchanan Maheshwari popularised the use of embryological characters in taxonomy. He is also known as 'The Father of Indian Plant Embryology'.
subject: Biology

question_text: Water is heated with a coil of resistance R connected to domestic supply. The rise of temperature of water will depend on 1. supply voltage 2. current passing through the coil 3. time for which voltage is supplied. Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
explanation: Heat generated by a resistance coil is given by H = I^2Rt. From Ohm's law, I = V/R. So, H = (V/R)^2 Rt = V^2t/R. Thus, it depends on voltage, current, and time.
subject: Physics

question_text: A pendulum clock is lifted to a height where the gravitational acceleration has a certain value of g. Another pendulum clock of same length, but of double the mass of the bob is lifted to another height where the gravitational acceleration is g/2. The time period of the second pendulum would be (in terms of period T of the first pendulum)
explanation: Time period of a pendulum, T = 2 * pi * sqrt(l/g). When acceleration due to gravity changed to g/2, then time period, T' = 2 * pi * sqrt(l/(g/2)) = sqrt(2) * (2 * pi * sqrt(l/g)) = sqrt(2) * T.
subject: Physics

question_text: The loudness of sound depends upon the
options: velocity of sound waves in the medium
frequency and velocity of the sound waves
explanation: Loudness of sound is depend on its amplitude, while sharpness of sound wave is depend on its frequency.
subject: Physics

question_text: Two bodies of mass M each are placed R distance apart. In another system, two bodies of mass 2M each are placed R/2 distance apart. If F be the gravitational force between the bodies in the first system, then the bodies in the second system will be
explanation: Situation I: F = GMM/R^2. Situation II: F' = G(2M)(2M)/(R/2)^2 = 4GM^2 / (R^2/4) = 16GM^2/R^2 = 16F.
subject: Physics

question_text: Light rays move in straight lines. But through an optical fibre, they can move in any type of zig-zag path because
options: the holes through the fibres are extremely fine
light rays are absorbed at the entry end and relieved at the exit end of the fibre
scattering of light occurs inside the fibre
successive total internal reflections occur as a ray moves through the fibre
explanation: The working of optical fibre is based on the total internal reflection. Its inner part is core of higher refractive index surrounded by another layer of glass of lower refractive index. It is surrounded by plastic jacket. When light enters from the one end of the core and moves towards cladding, then total internal reflection takes place again and again and light propagate through it.
subject: Physics

question_text: Which one of the following statements regarding cathode rays is not correct?
options: Cathode ray particles start from anode and move towards cathode.
In the absence of electrical and magnetic fields, cathode rays travel in straight lines.
Television picture tubes are cathode ray tubes.
explanation: Cathode rays start from cathode and move towards anode, because they are made of negatively charged electrons.
subject: Physics

question_text: A very large volume of hydrogen can be accommodated by making
explanation: A very large volume of hydrogen can be accommodated by making non-stoichiometric hydrides. Such hydrides are formed by some of the metals (e.g. Pd, Pt). This property of hydrogen has high potential for hydrogen storage.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Which one of the following is not a monoatomic element?
explanation: Among the given species, only iodine is not a monoatomic element. It exists in the form of I2 (diatomic), while rest occur as monoatomic element.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Which one of the following represents the correct order of electron releasing tendency of metals?
explanation: The correct order of electron releasing tendency of given metals is Zn > Cu > Ag. This can be explained on the basis of standard reduction potentials of given elements. More negative be the E_red value, greater is the tendency of element to release electron. Zn has highly negative E_red value, while Cu has least negative E_red value.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Which one of the following is the major constituent of biogas?
explanation: Biogas usually contains 45-70% methane and 30-45% carbon dioxide. It also contains small amounts of nitrogen, hydrogen sulphide, halogenated compound and organic silicon compounds. Thus, among the given options, methane is the major constituent of biogas.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Thyroid gland produces a hormone called 'thyroxine' which
explanation: Thyroid gland produces a hormone called thyroxine, which controls the metabolic rate of the body. It acts to increase the basal metabolic rate and affects protein, fat and carbohydrate metabolism affecting how human cells use energetic compounds.
subject: Biology

question_text: Which one of the following is a bacterium that causes disease in the human body?
explanation: Salmonella typhi is a bacterium which causes typhoid fever in the human body. This fever is contracted by the ingestion of contaminated food and water. Varicella zoster is a virus causing chickenpox. Trypanosoma gambiense and Plasmodium falciparum are protozoans which cause sleeping-sickness and malaria, respectively in the human body.
subject: Biology

question_text: Which one of the following statements regarding viruses is not true?
options: Viruses need living cells to reproduce
Viruses can synthesise their food through photosynthesis
Viruses are similar to chemical substances outside the host
correct_answer: Viruses can synthesise their food through photosynthesis
explanation: The statement given in option (c) is not true and can be corrected as Viruses do not perform photosynthesis to synthesise their food. They are inert, crystalline structure outside the living cell. Once they infect a cell, they takeover the machinery of the host cell to replicate themselves, killing the host. Rest of the statements are correct.
subject: Biology

question_text: Which one of the following diseases may be caused by the deficiency of vitamin-C?
explanation: The deficiency of vitamin-C (ascorbic acid) causes scurvy. This condition is characterised by general weakness, anaemia, gingivitis and skin haemorrhage.
subject: Biology

question_text: Compared to audible sound waves, ultrasound waves have
explanation: Ultrasound waves have higher frequency than audible sound waves. The audible range of sound for human beings is form 20 to 20,000 Hz. Children under the age of 5 and some animals such as dogs can hear upto 25,000 Hz. As people grow older, their ears become less sensitive to higher frequency. Ultrasonic sound of frequency higher than 20,000 Hz, which cannot be heard by human beings.
subject: Physics

question_text: A rigid body of mass 2 kg is dropped from a stationary balloon kept at a height of 50 m from the ground. The speed of the body when it just touches the ground and the total energy when it is dropped from the balloon are respectively.
explanation: Given, M = 2 kg and height = 50 m. Speed of body at the ground, v^2 - u^2 = 2gH => v = sqrt(2gH) [u=0] => v = sqrt(2 * 9.8 * 50) => v = sqrt(980) ms^-1. Hence, the total energy = kinetic energy => TE = 1/2 * M * v^2 => TE = 1/2 * 2 * (sqrt(980))^2 = 980 J. Hence, (d) is correct.
subject: Physics

question_text: The temperature of a place on one sunny day is 113 in Fahrenheit scale. The Kelvin scale reading of this temperature will be
explanation: Given, temperature, Tf = 113 F. As, we know Tk = 273 + 10/18 * (Tf - 32) => Tk = 273 + 10/18 * (113 - 32) => Tk = 318 K.
subject: Physics

question_text: Radiations coming from the sun are mostly in the form of
options: Both short and long wavelength infrared
explanation: The mode of transfer of heat from one body to another without any actual movement the particles involved and without heating the intervening medium, is called radiation. For radiation, there is no need of any medium because it is of electromagnetic nature. So, radiation coming from the sun are mostly in form of light and long wavelength infrared.
subject: Physics

question_text: In the Manusmriti which form of marriage results from the 'Voluntary union of a maiden and her lover'?
explanation: In the Manusmriti, fifth (Gandharva form of marriage) results from the 'Voluntary union of a maiden and her lover'.
subject: History

question_text: Which one of the following is a Rabi crop in the Northern States of India?
explanation: Rabi crops are winter crops which are sown in October-November and harvested in March. The Rabi crops in Northern states of India includes Barley, wheat, oats, gram, linseed and mustard.
subject: Geography

question_text: The rivers of North-West Europe are good examples of
explanation: The rivers of North-West Europe are good examples of barbed drainage pattern. Barbed drainage pattern is a rare kind of drainage pattern which is formed when the tributaries flow in opposite direction to their master streams.
subject: Geography

question_text: Which one of the following ocean currents is a cold current?
explanation: South Atlantic Drift/Current is an eastward flowing cold ocean current, fed by the Brazil Current. It is continuous with the northern edge of the Antarctic Circumpolar Current.
subject: Geography

question_text: Paradip Port is located on the delta of river
explanation: It is a natural, deep-water port on the East coast of India in Jagatsinghpur district of Odisha. Paradip Port is situated at confluence of the Mahanadi river and the Bay of Bengal.
subject: Geography

question_text: Which one of the following hypothesis/theory explains the origin of the Universe?
explanation: Nebular Hypothesis was given by Immanuel Kant to explain the origin of the Universe.
subject: Geography

question_text: Which among the following struggles, based on Gandhi's philosophy of Satyagraha, involved the industrial working class?
explanation: Ahmedabad Mill Strike, 1918 was based on Gandhi's philosophy of Satyagraha, that involved the industrial working class. The industrial dispute for wage hike was between the owners and workers of a cotton mill in Ahmedabad.
subject: History

question_text: Consider the following statements related to the Virashaiva tradition of Karnataka. 1. The Virashaiva Movement was led by a Brahmana named Basavanna, a minister in the court of the Kalachuri ruler in the twelfth century. 2. The Virashaivas encouraged practices, approved by the Dharmashastras, like post-puberty marriage and remarriage of widows. Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
explanation: The twelfth century witnessed the emergence of a new movement called Virashaiva Movement in Karnataka. The movement was led by a Brahmana named Basavanna (1106-68) who was initially a Jaina and a minister in the court of a Kalachuri ruler. Also, the Dharmashastras did not permit widow remarriages and post-puberty marriages. But the Virashaivas undertook them as a sign of refusal of the sacred Brahmanical scriptures.
subject: History

question_text:
Consider the following statements related to Wellesley's administration.
1. In the six years of Wellesley's administration, the army accounted for 42.5% of the Company's total expenditure.
2. Wellesley's administrative measures were restricted to the affairs to the Company and had nothing to do with the commercial and military affairs of the Indian ruling families.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
explanation:
During Lord Wellesley's tenure, army was an expensive machinery of the British East India Company. He had waged war on many Princely States and native rulers like Mysore, Marathas, Nizams etc. Hence, to sustain such a larger army, he spent huge amounts (42.5% of the company's total expenditure) on army. He also devised the infamous Subsidiary Alliance System which required to maintain British army in native ruler's courts. Hence, statement (1) is correct.
Wellesley was an excellent administrator. He used his Subsidiary Alliance System to interfere with the commercial and military affairs to Indian rulers by making them mandatorily consult him on important decisions.
Hence, statements (2) is also correct.
subject: History

question_text:
Consider the following statements concerning the Russian Revolution.
1. The Bolsheviks believed that in a repressive society like Tsarist Russia, the party should be disciplined and should control the number of its members.
2. The Mensheviks believed that the party should be opened to all (as in Germany).
Selects the correct answer using the codes given below.
explanation:
The Bolsheviks and Mensheviks were the two factions of Russian Social Democratic Labour Party formed under leaderships of Vladimir Lenin and Julius Martov respectively.
Bolsheviks believed in limiting the membership of party to a core professional member body as it was easier to manage them which was necessary in a repressive society like Tsarist Russia.
Hence, statement (1) is correct.
On the other hand Mensheviks believed in power of masses and advocated liberal thoughts like entry of common masses in the party. Hence, statement (2) is also correct.
subject: History

question_text:
Which of the following was/were among the decisions taken by the First Continental Congress held in Philadelphia in September, 1774?
1. It rejected a plan for a colonial union under the British authority.
2. It drew up a statement of grievances.
3. It agreed upon a scheme to stop trade between the Colonies and England.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
explanation:
The First Continental Congress held in Philadelphia in September, 1774 is a major landmark in the history of USA. It was attended by representatives of 12 out of 13 British Colonies in USA, at the Carpenter's Hall. It was held in response to British impasses over the historic Boston Tea Party of December, 1773.
The major outcomes of this Congress were
• Rejection of Union of colonies under British Crown.
• Scheme for boycott of trade between the colonies and the Britishers.
• Mechanism of grievance discussion.
Hence, all the statements are correct.
subject: History

question_text: Which one of the following land territories of Indonesia is not touched by the Equator?
explanation: Java island is located to the South of equator at around 5°S latitude in a West to East orientation, so Java is not touched by the equator. However, equator passes through the Sumatra, Sulawesi and Kalimantan portion of Borneo island in Indonesia.

question_text: Which one of the following sedimentary rocks is organically formed?
explanation:
Organically formed sedimentary rocks are formed from the remains of living organisms such as corals & shell fish (calcareous rock); or from vegetative remains like forests & swamps (carbonaceous rocks). Some examples of organically formed sedimentary rocks are chalk, limestone, peat, lignite & coal.
Shale is a mechanically formed sedimentary rock. Halite & chert are chemically formed sedimentary rocks.
subject: Geography

question_text: According to the Koppen climatic classification, the letter code Cfa denotes.
explanation:
Koeppen's climate classification is based on annual & monthy average temperatures and precipitation. According to this classification Cfa denotes Humid subtropical climate.
This type of climate is characterised by warm summer and absence of dry season. Tropical wet climate is denoted by Af; Tundra climate is denoted by ET and Tropical wet & dry climate is denoted by Aw.
subject: Geography

question_text: In which one of the following folds in the axial plane found to be virtually horizontal?
explanation:
In recumbent fold, aecial plane found to be horizontal. The axial plane of a fold is the plane or surface that divides the fold as symmetrically as possible.
In Isoclinal fold, the axial surface and limbs slope in the same direction and at approximately the same angle.
An Anticlinal fold is an arch like fold which is convex upward.
Monoclinal fold is a step-like fold consisting of a zone of steeper dip within or otherwise horizontal topography.
subject: Geography

question_text: How many Ramsar convention sites have been enlisted from India so far?
explanation:
Has 27 Ramsar sites like Dal lake, Pong Dam, Harike Wetland, Chilika lake etc.
Ramsar Convention on Wetlands is an international treaty on conservation and sustainable use of Wetlands. It was signed in Ramsar, a city in Iran in 1971.
India Chilika lake was first to be designated as a Ramsar site in India.

question_text: Which one of the following statements about the Suez Canal is not correct?
options: The Suez Canal was constructed in 1869.
It links the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea.
It has a six lock system and ships cross the different levels through these locks.
It has given Europe a new gateway to the Indian Ocean.
correct_answer: It has a six lock system and ships cross the different levels through these locks.
explanation: The Suez Canal has no lock system as the water level in the Mediterranean Sea and Red Sea is nearly the same.

question_text: Which among the following statements is not correct about the Reign of Terror?
options: The Jacobins dashed out the Girondists with the help of Sans-Culottes.
The Jacobins were in league with the French clergy.
The arrest for anti-revolutionary activities was by law restricted to the political class.
The Reign of Terror came to an end with the execution of Robespierre by guillotine in July, 1794.
correct_answer: The Jacobins were in league with the French clergy.
explanation: The Jacobins were not in league with the French clergy; they were associated with the Sans-Culottes.

question_text: Who among the following was the first Indian to qualify for the Indian Civil Service?
explanation: Satyendranath Tagore was the first Indian to join the Indian Civil Service. He was selected in 1863.
subject: History

question_text: Which among the following was/were among the factors for England to experience the Industrial Revolution first? 1. The scientific inventions had paved the way for Industrial Revolution. 2. It had favourable social and political structures in place. 3. Navigable rivers had made inland transport easier. 4. It had seen the ascendancy of capitalist practices.
explanation: All listed factors (scientific inventions, social/political structures, navigable rivers, and capitalist practices) contributed to England experiencing the Industrial Revolution first.
subject: History

question_text: Article-46 of the Constitution of India refers to the promotion of educational and economic interests of
options: Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections
displaced persons from large irrigation projects
correct_answer: Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections
explanation: Article 46 specifically mentions the promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other weaker sections.

question_text: Who was the Education Minister in the first Cabinet of Independent India?
explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was the Education Minister in the first Cabinet of Independent India.

question_text: Who among the following died in exile?
explanation: Bahadur Shah Zafar died in exile in Rangoon in 1862.

question_text: The normal lapse rate of temperature of Earth's atmosphere drops to 0°C at the
explanation: The normal lapse rate of temperature of Earth's atmosphere drops to 0°C at the upper boundary of the tropopause.

question_text: The headquarters of National Research Laboratory for Conservation of Cultural Property (NRLC) is located at
explanation: The National Research Laboratory for Conservation of Cultural Property (NRLC) is located at Lucknow.

question_text: Loktak lake is situated in the State of
explanation: Loktak Lake is located at Moirang in Manipur, India. It is the largest fresh water lake of North-East India & is famous for phumdis (floating vegetative mass). Keibul Lamjao National Park, one of the phumdis of the Lake, is the only floating national park in the world. It is also the last natural habitat of endangered Sangai deer.

question_text: Stalactite, stalagmite and pillars are the depositional landforms of
explanation: Stalactite and stalagmite and pillars are the depositional landforms of underground water. Stalactite and stalagmite are formed when the calcium carbonate dissolved in groundwater.

question_text: A deep valley characterised by steep step like slope is known as
explanation: Canyon is a deep valley characterised by steep step like slopes. A U-shaped valley is a glaciated landform having a characteristic U-shape with steep straight sides & a flat or rounded bottom. A blind valley is a deep, narrow & flat bottomed valley with an abrupt ending. A Gorge is a deep, narrow valley with steep sides.

question_text: Which one of the following is a major plate?
explanation: Among the given options, Pacific plate is a major plate. The outer shell of Earth, Lithosphere is broken into tectonic plates. There are seven major tectonic plates which include Pacific Plate, North American Plate, Eurasian Plate, African Plate, Antarctic Plate, Indo-Australian Plate and South American Plate. There are about 20 minor plates including Cocos Plate, Nazca plate Arabian Plate Philippine plate and Caroline Plate etc.
